subject: English Language
labelling_note: This library PDF is the 2024 sample paper, as stated on its cover. The listening passage is not included in the pupil’s paper; its answers were checked against the accompanying TETEA sample solutions.

questions.prompt: Who took Uadilifu to hospital?
steps: Identify the person who accompanied the patient, rather than the hospital staff.
The checked listening answers identify Uadilifu’s mother.

questions.prompt: What happened to the doctor’s family after he was jailed?
steps: Focus on the family’s circumstances after the imprisonment.
The consequence was difficulty obtaining everyday necessities, rather than the family also being imprisoned.

questions.prompt: What did the doctor demand before treating Uadilifu?
steps: Distinguish a lawful salary from an unofficial payment demanded for a service.
The doctor was asking for an unlawful payment.

questions.prompt: Why did the doctor delay attending to Uadilifu?
steps: Connect the delay with the demand described in the preceding item.
Treatment was withheld until an unofficial payment was made.

questions.prompt: Why is corruption harmful?
steps: Consider how demanding money affects access to essential public services.
A person who cannot make the unofficial payment may be refused a service they are entitled to receive.
questions.answer: B — It denies people their basic rights.

questions.prompt: The boys saw a snake and ran ___ a nearby room.
steps: The sentence describes movement from outside to inside.
Use the preposition into for entry into an enclosed place.

questions.prompt: Here is the book ___ was written by Mwalimu J. K. Nyerere.
steps: The relative pronoun refers to the thing book.
Which can introduce a clause describing a thing.

questions.prompt: Upendo prefers singing ___ playing netball.
steps: Use the pattern prefer one activity to another.
Both activities are expressed with -ing forms.

questions.prompt: The lost ball belongs to me: The lost ball is ___.
steps: The answer stands alone after is, without a following noun.
Use the possessive pronoun mine; my must be followed by a noun.

questions.prompt: Add a confirmation tag to: You all ate a lot yesterday.
steps: Ate is a positive simple-past verb, so use the negative auxiliary didn’t.
Keep the same subject pronoun you.

questions.prompt: My neighbour’s laziness caused him to live a ___ life.
steps: Choose an adjective to describe life.
The negative consequence of laziness fits miserable, meaning unhappy or very uncomfortable.

questions.prompt: They thought drinking would make them feel ___, until they became unhealthy.
steps: The first part states their expectation; the later part contrasts with it.
Good describes the positive feeling they expected.

questions.prompt: Neema grows maize on a ten-acre farm, and the ___ improved yearly.
steps: Look for the noun naming crops collected from farming.
Harvest is the crop yield gathered from the farm.

questions.prompt: Bahati wept because she could not control her own ___.
steps: A possessive adjective such as her own needs a noun after it.
Misfortune means bad luck or an unfortunate event and explains her distress.

questions.prompt: I ___ that I would never lie again. Choose from the printed word bank.
steps: A finite past-tense verb is required before that.
Admitted is the available past-tense reporting verb; the other options do not fit this structure.
questions.tip: Promised would be more natural for a commitment about future behaviour, but it is not in the supplied word bank.

questions.prompt: Match the place where sick people receive medical treatment.
steps: Identify the service: care and treatment for ill people.
A hospital supplies that service.

questions.prompt: Match the place where pupils receive education.
steps: Identify the activity as organised teaching and learning.
That place is a school.

questions.prompt: Match a place where one buys a meal.
steps: A prepared meal is bought and served in a restaurant.
Choose the option for that eating place.

questions.prompt: Match the place for reading and borrowing books.
steps: The important clue is borrowing books.
A library lends books and provides reading space.

questions.prompt: Match the place where milk is sold.
steps: A dairy supplies milk and dairy products.
Select dairy rather than unrelated institutions such as a bank or mint.

questions.prompt: The Director is (provide) ___ the reward to his employees.
steps: Is introduces the present continuous: is + verb-ing.
Remove the final e from provide, then add -ing.

questions.prompt: If my mother (wake up) ___ early, she will catch the bus.
steps: A first conditional uses present simple after if and will in the main clause.
Mother is third-person singular, so wake becomes wakes.

questions.prompt: Have Bahati and Jema (speak) ___ to their teacher yet?
steps: Have introduces the present perfect, which requires a past participle.
The forms are speak, spoke, spoken.

questions.prompt: My children rarely (play) ___ with their toys.
steps: Rarely describes a habit, so use present simple.
Children is plural: use the base form play, without -s.

questions.prompt: He checked the tube by (put) ___ it into water.
steps: After the preposition by, use the -ing form.
Double the final t in put before adding -ing.

questions.prompt: What is the poem about?
steps: Notice the repeated question about what the speaker wants to do in life.
Each stanza names a future profession and explains its benefit to other people.
questions.answer: It is about career ambitions and serving the community.

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker want to become a lawyer?
steps: Read the first stanza’s reasons for choosing law.
The speaker connects that profession with children who have suffered abuse and people’s rights.
questions.answer: To help abused children and defend people’s rights.

questions.prompt: What kind of person is the speaker?
steps: Use the motives in all three stanzas as evidence.
The speaker puts other people’s welfare, protection and health first.
questions.answer: A caring, responsible and ambitious person.
questions.tip: Support character descriptions with actions or ideas from the poem.

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker ask, If not me, who else?
steps: This repeated rhetorical question does not request a person’s name.
It emphasises that the speaker should take personal responsibility rather than wait for someone else.
questions.answer: To express personal responsibility and readiness to help others.

questions.prompt: Suggest a suitable title.
steps: Choose a short title covering the shared idea across all three careers.
A title about future ambitions fits the whole poem.
questions.tip: Other relevant titles, such as Serving My Community, can also earn credit.

questions.prompt: Fill in the pupil’s name on Misongo’s identity card.
steps: Find the full name in the opening sentence.
Copy both names with initial capital letters.

questions.prompt: Fill in the school.
steps: Find the institution named in the description.
Write its full name rather than shortening it to Upepo.

questions.prompt: Fill in the class.
steps: Read the class stated in the question.
Use the stated information even though the dates and class in the sample are unusual.

questions.prompt: Fill in the date of birth.
steps: Select the birth date, not the school entry date.
Write the day, month and year clearly.

questions.prompt: Fill in the school entry date.
steps: Find the date describing his first day at school.
Keep it separate from the birth date.

summaries.Section A — Listening: Listen for who, what happened and why. Keep actions, motives and consequences separate.
summaries.Section A — Grammar: Choose pronouns by what they replace, prepositions by meaning, and question tags by tense and subject.
summaries.Section A — Vocabulary: Check meaning and grammatical function before selecting from a word bank.
summaries.Section A — Places: Match each service to the institution that provides it.
summaries.Section B — Verb forms: Use present continuous after is, the present simple after if in a first conditional, and a participle after have.
summaries.Section B — Poetry: Use the speaker’s repeated ideas and stated motives to support interpretations. Suitable alternative wording is acceptable.
summaries.Section C — Identity card: Copy the given facts into the correct fields. Do not invent different dates to repair the sample’s unusual chronology.
